Setup (per docs/research/variance_of_associator.md § "Worked example:
single Fano generator"):
A(a, b, c) := ‖[a, b, c]‖²   where [a,b,c] = (a·b)·c − a·(b·c)
Unperturbed: [a,b,c] = 2·e_7, A = 4.

variance (from the β document, derivation):
Var(A) ≈ 64 σ²                                (TRUTH)
If the current compiler's stepwise scalar-product rule were applied
instead, it would give:
Var_compiler(A) ≈ 16 σ²                       (COMPILER, 4× low)
This test computes the sample variance of A over N = 100,000 Monte
Carlo samples and compares to the TRUTH formula. It does NOT test the
compiler's variance_of() — that requires the full Knowledge<f64>
chain which introduces unrelated complexities (see ζ buffer bug). The
compiler comparison is deferred to a separate test.
Pass criterion: |MC_var − 64σ²| / 64σ² < 0.05 (5% relative error).
If this passes, β's analytical formula is validated empirically. The
remaining claim — that the compiler produces 16σ² — is then a
separate reading-confirmation task.

within-organ redistribution is instantaneous but Q-transport between
blood and tissue remains rate-limited. The hierarchy is
PBPK28-literature → PBPK14 → 1-state QSS
with monotonically decreasing model-form complexity. Discrepancies

1. Build adjacency matrix (synthetic connectome, 8 nodes)
2. Compute graph Laplacian
3. Extract 7 eigenvectors via deflated power iteration
4. Map eigenvectors to octonion basis (ψ_k ↔ e_k)
5. Compute G₂ 3-form on the eigenvector frame
6. Compute SU(3) branching quality
7. Run null model (random SO(7) rotations)
8. Compare observed vs null → p-value estimate

T3: Null distribution has lower mean |φ| than observed

T5: Associator deviation field computable on extracted frame

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `knowledge_layout_shadows_user_field_name`. A user struct field named `value` was silently clobbered by its sibling. `ir_register_knowledge_layout` preseeds a synthetic `Knowledge` layout — value@0, variance@1, confidence@2 — as entry 0 of the struct layout table,. description: A user struct field named `value` was silently clobbered by its sibling. `ir_register_knowledge_layout` preseeds a synthetic `Knowledge` layout — value@0, variance@1, confidence@2 — as entry 0 of the struct layout table,
comments: A user struct field named `value` was silently clobbered by its sibling.
`ir_register_knowledge_layout` preseeds a synthetic `Knowledge` layout —
value@0, variance@1, confidence@2 — as entry 0 of the struct layout table,
before any user struct is registered. `field_idx_from_name_simple` resolves a
field *name* to a slot by scanning the whole table in order and taking the
first hit in any struct, and that path is what runs whenever the base is not
a typed local: `arr[i].f` reaches it because array locals record a length but
no element type.
So `ext[0].value` resolved to Knowledge's slot 0 — the same slot as `oid` —
and `ext[0].value = val_buf` overwrote the `oid` written just before it. Both
reads then went to slot 0 too, so `value` read back correct while `oid`
returned `value`'s bytes: a silent wrong answer at rc=0, with no diagnostic.
The trigger was the identifier, not the shape. The same program with the
field named `val` was always correct, at any struct size, array length or
index form — which is why size- and index-threshold hypotheses all died.
Guard all three preseeded names. Anything reading its sibling's data here
means the synthetic layout is shadowing user layouts again.
Honest scope: CI runs this suite under souc-stage2, which never carried the
defect, so this file is green either way there — it is the readable witness,
not the guard. The discriminating gate is the `knowledge_field_shadow` case
in tests/madaros/source_to_elf/manifest.tsv, which compiles with Madaros and
was measured red before this fix and green after.

PROVED the identical hole was still live for while/for loop bodies:
var x = measure(1)                        // {s1}
while i<3 { x = x + measure(2); i=i+1 }    // inside: union={s1,s2}
let y = x + x                              // AFTER the loop: union=1

Root cause was the SAME as if/match: checker_check_block_inplace's
push_scope()/pop_scope() around the loop body discards any env rebind made
inside it, so the reassignment never reached anywhere outside the loop.
The fix wraps BOTH checker_check_while_expr_inplace and
checker_check_for_in_expr_inplace with the SAME checker_ns_branch_enter_
inplace (before the body) / checker_merge_ns_reassigned_inplace (after)
pair used for if/match -- they do NOT share a single body-check function
(each is its own top-level expr handler calling
checker_check_opt_block_inplace independently), so both needed their own
wrap. A loop body runs 0+ times and accumulates, so the sound post-loop
value for any Knowledge var reassigned in the body is TOP (widen) --
identical hammer to if/match, deliberately NOT a per-binding fixpoint
union (no such pass exists, or is being added, here).
Two probes below, while and for, each: measure a fresh value, reassign a
pre-loop Knowledge var to it INSIDE the loop body, then read the var again
AFTER the loop (`x + x` / `z + z`) -- the end-to-end proof that the
forced-top value survived past the loop, not just that the merge ran.
Observable only under SOUNIO_NS_TRACE=1: both post-loop unions MUST read
"NS_TRACE union=-1" (top), NOT the pre-loop variable's own original handle.
Per-rule sabotage: SOUNIO_NS_SABOTAGE_JOIN=1 (same knob as if/match)
disables the loop merge too, reproducing the exact fail-open grok-4.6
measured: both post-loop unions revert to the PRE-loop handle instead of
top.

M_n = M_0 at every step, three drug profiles, dt ∈ {0.5, 0.1, 0.05} h.

state (CN alone would: it rings to −9 mg/L here, which is why it is not
the production path). TR-BDF2's internal stage x_γ is printed as

clearance on the liver, CL_form·dt/V_liver ≈ 12 at dt = 0.5 h), the
ledger identity M(T) + eliminated + sink_removed − administered = M(0)
closes to rounding under a constant input.
4. The same with the input routed into the liver's vascular space
(portal first-pass, input_organ = 1): the identity still closes, and
routing through the liver raises the liver AUC over blood input.
Bounds (theta_pbpk28 gate functions): |ΔM|/M_0 ≤ max(1e-12, steps·1e-15),
a heuristic rounding budget for an identity that is exact in real
arithmetic; booked negative mass ≤ 5e-7 mg, half the last digit of a

The ZD-geometry report (SEDENION_ZERO_DIVISOR_GEOMETRY_REPORT.md) left this OPEN: it found the
zero-divisor side has no factor 11, and conjectured "the 11 in 1848 = 11*168 belongs to the
associator side". This test EXECUTES the associator side and confirms it exactly.
For sedenion basis units e_i, e_j, e_k the associator [e_i,e_j,e_k] = (e_i e_j)e_k - e_i(e_j e_k)
is a single component e_(i^j^k) with integer coefficient
A(i,j,k) = sigma(i,j)*sigma(i^j,k) - sigma(j,k)*sigma(i,j^k)   in {-2, 0, +2}.
A triple is non-associative iff A != 0. Over the 15*14*13 = 2730 ORDERED distinct triples of
imaginary units {1..15}:
* exactly 1848 are non-associative, and 1848 = 11 * 168 = 11 * |PSL(2,7)|;
* by output grade s = i^j^k: each of the 14 grades s != 8 carries exactly 120, and the doubling
grade s = 8 carries 168 (= the octonion associator count). So 1848 = 14*120 + 168 = 10*168 + 168,
i.e. the "11" splits as 11 = 10 + 1 (the doubling grade contributes the +1*168);
* the octonion sub-tower {1..7} contributes exactly 168 ordered non-associative triples.
Decidable integer arithmetic, no float. SELF-CONTAINED. Cross-verified vs
scripts/research/sedenion_associator_1848_oracle.py by scripts/ci/sedenion_associator_1848_gate.sh

that builds the suite's stage2 binary has no such classification and reads

Reading a Seq<f64> element must produce a float, in every spelling.
Seq access is an intrinsic: `seq.get(i)` lowers to __sounio_seq_get with no
fn symbol, so the two routines that classify an expression's type both missed
on the mangled-method lookup and fell through to their integer default:
expr_result_scalar_kind_ref (println) and expr_result_is_float_ref
(arithmetic). The `a[i]` spelling had an answer in both; the method spelling
had one in neither.
Measured on the committed compiler before the fix -- a wrong-code path, not a
rejection, so the program type-checked clean and printed nonsense:
println(w.get(0))               -> refused, "unresolved scalar kind"
Seq<i64> was correct throughout the same shapes, which is what made this a
float-classification defect rather than a Seq defect.
NOT covered here: a `&Seq<T>` PARAMETER. That path is separate, and it was
broken -- reading one indirection level off -- until 2026-09-09. It was not a
pre-existing defect: the reference-receiver fix in PR #2413 made the call

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `tuple_one_slot_struct_borrow`. &t.N / &!t.N on a tuple element that is a ONE-FIELD struct must not crash. It should compile and run successfully.
description: &t.N / &!t.N on a tuple element that is a ONE-FIELD struct must not crash
comments: tuple_borrow_elem_resolve() (fix for &t.0 / &!t.0 generally) resolves a tuple element's
address and type, but every element wider than one slot is copied inline by the tuple
constructor while a ONE-slot struct element is stored as the struct's value in rax --
a pointer to its data, not the cell holding a pointer. Taking that cell's address (as
every other element kind wants) yields a pointer to a pointer; the first read through
it dereferences garbage and segfaults.
Scope: locally built tuples only. A one-field struct inside a tuple RETURNED from a
function is its own, separate, older, pre-existing bug -- the pointer such an element
holds is into the callee's dead frame, so it is garbage after the next call whether or
not any borrow is involved (`let a = mk_one(); other_call(); a.0.n` reads garbage with
zero borrows in play). That bug is not fixed here; this test avoids it by only
constructing the one-field-struct tuples in `main`'s own frame.
Scope: local variables only (x86). Global tuple variables have a separate, pre-existing
issue with tuple-typed globals unrelated to element width, so a one-field struct in a
global tuple is not covered here either.

comments: Regression for the i64 type-hash overflow on 3-level pointer nesting
(closed in 2523ee2f4 by composite-type interning in lean_single.sio).
Pre-fix: ref_hash_make compounded the inner hash by *256 per level while
the inner still carried the 2^50 band, so &Option<Box<Struct>> wrapped
mod 2^64 and corrupted the struct hash — field access reported
"unknown field" and shapes collided.
Post-fix: composite inners are interned (CT_INNER_HASH[4096]) and only
a small surrogate id is multiplied, keeping the encoded hash inside
[2^50, 2^51) at arbitrary depth.
This fixture exercises field access through two structurally distinct
3-level nestings simultaneously to assert they do not alias: the same
compile unit creates and reads both &Option<Box<A>> and &Option<Box<B>>.
Under the bug, the two struct hashes would collide after the ×256 wrap
(different inner structs, same wrapped surrogate), so the field offsets
would be wrong for at least one of them.
